properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's words, 2026-10-29: "one of the goals of AI has been AGI, but to me, having the agent do absolutely everything might be the wrong approach. Being able to allow the agent to have a "notepad" (aka reflow2), may allow AGI, just not via strictly an agent. Instead, an agent can be very good at "reasoning" or what I'll call "cognition", and reflow2, can be the sketchpad/notepad the agent can use instead of having to rely on ultra long and complex context window... we'll call reflow2 the "memory". Between them, maybe AGI is more possible."

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) A FRAMING: say it as how reflow2 sees itself (cognition is the agent's, memory is reflow2's), beside the accepted rule that reflow2 is one of three parts and does not compete with the others.
(b) A LINE OF REASONING: record it as an argument in its own design, with premises, the objections below and the evidence the trials produce, as a sibling of the proof thesis.
(c) A MEASUREMENT: tasks too long or too tangled for one context window, the same agent with and without reflow2, counted. The general form of the proof thesis's A/B test.
(d) A MAP OF MEMORY KINDS: lay out what reflow2 already holds as working memory (the read-back), long-term facts (the design), history (changes), know-how (skills, rules, lessons), and what it lacks (forgetting, consolidating, and knowing what to recall).

PUSHBACK:
- THE HUMAN DROPS OUT OF THIS FRAMING. The proof thesis was "human + ai agent + reflow2", and the accepted rule names three parts. Whether the person is a third part of the intelligence, or its owner outside it, is part of the question.
- MEMORY WRITTEN IS NOT MEMORY USED. reflow2's own design has measured this repeatedly: a rule broken the same day it was ruled on, and lessons filed in one place that did not change the next call until they were served at the step they concern. The hard part of a two-part mind is recall: knowing what to read, and when.
- THE SHAPE IS NOT NEW. The extended-mind thesis in philosophy, cognitive architectures that split memory from reasoning, and agent memory systems built on retrieval all pair reasoning with outside memory. What reflow2 adds is memory that is typed and checks itself (what follows, what conflicts, what is owed), not a pile of notes. That difference is the claim worth testing.
- NOTHING LEARNS. The agent's own reasoning does not get better from what reflow2 holds; only what it is handed does. Whether that counts as general intelligence is a definition question.
- "AGI" HAS NO AGREED TEST. A claim about it cannot be checked as stated; (c) gives a measurable version.

COST (a finding): (a) a sentence; (d) small, a read of what exists; (b) small; (c) moderate, and the only one that can show it wrong.
properties.name: OPEN — is general intelligence more reachable as two parts, an agent good at reasoning ("cognition") and reflow2 as its written memory, than as one model that does everything inside an ever longer context?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's generalisation of the proof thesis recorded beside it the same day: the division of labour he proposed for unfinished proofs, applied to intelligence in general.
